note: Expected values are frozen, hand-reviewed control points with two documented provenance classes. Class 'pyproj_frozen_transverse_mercator' (UTM points): plain transverse-mercator conversions with no datum-shift grids involved, deterministic across PROJ versions; values frozen once and re-proven by the engine. Class 'epsg_method_1024_equations' (EPSG:3857 points): values derived analytically from the published spherical-Mercator equations — independent of any transformation library, re-provable even where pyproj is absent (pure-Python Termux track). A mismatch beyond tolerance is a hard error: the layer must refuse to trust its transformation engine or its reference, not adjust the reference.
tolerance_note: Forward checks: metres — UTM tolerance 0.001 m (mm-level frozen values); EPSG:3857 tolerance 1e-6 m (equation re-derivation is exact on one platform; 1e-6 m absorbs cross-platform libm drift of ~1 ulp, observed engine-vs-equation diff is ~1e-9 m). Round-trip checks: degrees — UTM closure 1e-7, EPSG:3857 closure 1e-12 (observed closure error over a full grid is ~3e-14 deg).

references.epsg_3857: EPSG:3857 'WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator', EPSG method 1024 'Popular Visualisation Pseudo Mercator', formulas per EPSG Guidance Note 7-2: X = R*lambda, Y = R*ln[tan(pi/4 + phi/2)], R = 6378137 m (WGS84 semi-major axis); inverse phi = 2*atan(exp(Y/R)) - pi/2
references.epsg_utm: EPSG:32637/32638/32639 'WGS 84 / UTM zone 37N/38N/39N', transverse mercator without datum-shift grids (deterministic across PROJ versions)
references.vertical_crs: Vertical references verified against the EPSG database shipped with PROJ: EPSG:5714 'MSL height', EPSG:5773 'EGM96 height', EPSG:3855 'EGM2008 height', EPSG:5703 'NAVD88 height' (metre), EPSG:5621 'EVRF2007 height', EPSG:4979 'WGS 84' (Geographic 3D, ellipsoidal heights)
references.crs_model: ISO 19111:2019 (referencing by coordinates, incl. compound CRS) and OGC 18-010r7 'Well-known text representation of coordinate reference systems' (WKT2) — the representation the WKT VERTCS reader in data_layer/vertical.py parses
